comparison: Perfect match on claims C31-C32 regarding confidence-uncertainty relationship. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the quantitative linear relationship and consistency across conditions, while peer review notes that any initial questions were satisfactorily addressed during review.

Perfect match on claim C25 regarding RMSE analysis. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis (F-test, effect size), while peer review treats this as a supporting behavioral observation consistent with experimental manipulation rather than a primary finding.

Perfect match on methodological claims C18-C20, C64-C77. Both evaluations find the methods SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the approach follows best practices but lacks power analysis justification. Peer review praises the rigor and innovative design, noting that additional details provided during review strengthened reliability.

High overlap (11 shared claims) on core expectation-weighted perception findings. Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes model comparison statistics (2-4 sigma effects) and convergence diagnostics. Peer review confirms all three reviewers found the evidence compelling with solid computational modeling support. Peer R1 also includes claims C30, C39, C48 which OpenEval addresses separately in R2.

OpenEval R2 addresses claims C30, C39, C48 regarding Kalman filter vs RL model comparison, finding evidence SUPPORTED but noting the advantage was condition-dependent and 'short of significance' in some conditions. Peer R1 includes these claims in their broader SUPPORTED evaluation of core findings without specifically discussing the nuanced KF vs RL comparison.

Peer review identified concerns about clinical relevance claims (C22, C44-C46, C62), rating them UNCERTAIN because the study used healthy participants without clinical pain data. OpenEval did not produce a corresponding evaluation of these clinical extrapolation claims.

Peer review evaluated background literature and theoretical framework claims (C1, C3, C7-C16, C42, C50-C52, C54-C56, C58) as SUPPORTED, treating them as established context. OpenEval did not produce a corresponding evaluation of these background/theoretical claims.
